clue.text: Termination of savings account no longer bearing interest?

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter, so only the end of savings is used

parts.note: an account is a story or tale

explanation.surface: A bank's notice about a savings account that has stopped earning interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks financial, but the definition plays on dull: something no longer interesting has gone flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale news or jokes have lost their freshness and so hold nobody's attention any more.

clue.text: Violently return shoe

explanation.surface: Someone hurls back a shoe in anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling something back is to hurl it back hard; a slingback is a woman's shoe held by a strap round the heel.

clue.text: Tree with less on top, having been lopped

indicators.note: lopped means cut off at the top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: balder means having less hair on the head

explanation.surface: A tree that has been pruned now has less foliage at its crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less on top' seems to describe the pruned tree, but it means balder, with less hair; lopping its head removes the B.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Argument in market

explanation.surface: A row breaks out among traders at a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated exchange is a quarrel; a stock or corn exchange is a place where trading happens.

clue.text: Given stick about school committee I took charge of

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the punishment word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: given the stick means punished with a cane, caned
PTA is the parent-teacher association of a school

explanation.surface: A school governor recalls running a committee after being beaten at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given stick' sounds like encouragement or criticism, but here it is corporal punishment; 'about' is the container signal, with the PTA (the British parent-teacher association) plus I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain leads a team, so to have captained something is to have led or commanded it.

clue.text: Whip-round for classical writer

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, called the cat
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A collection is taken to honour an ancient author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' reads as a collection of money, but splits into whip and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman and author of works on farming and history.

clue.text: Cleric's position in former religious act initially ignored

parts.note: former means bygone, past

indicators.note: the initial letter of the worship word is left out

parts.note: worship is an act of religious devotion

explanation.surface: A clergyman's post was once held in a church service now neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, and the suffix makes it his office.

clue.text: Writer occupying rural cottage

indicators.note: the answer occupies, sits within, the two words rural cottage

explanation.surface: An author lives in a country cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist of Little Women.

clue.text: Big cheese from Italy on our menu looks odd

indicators.note: something that looks odd is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Italian cheese on a restaurant menu seems strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big cheese' suggests food on the menu, but it is a top person; Italian for number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is the most important person, which the Italian phrase for number one also means.

clue.text: Noble bird not entirely visible on a lake

indicators.note: only part of the bird can be seen, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a duck is a water bird
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: An aristocratic bird is partly hidden on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to a duke, so it describes nobility.

clue.text: Film company's taping pet shows

indicators.note: taping means recording, here containing, so the pet goes inside

parts.note: an indie is an independent film company; indie's gives INDIES
a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: A film studio's footage of a household pet is screened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taping' reads as filming but signals that INDIES holds CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to point it out or signal it.

clue.text: Funny business, how those blind creatures ended up?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the creatures lost their tails, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the three blind mice of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A joke asks what happened to some famously sightless animals.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the tails of the three blind mice, so MICE loses its tail, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic as an adjective means causing laughter, amusing.

clue.text: Composer, English? Yes and no

parts.note: Sir Edward, the light-opera composer, was English by birth but bore the surname of a different nationality

explanation.surface: A quiz asks whether a composer counts as English.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edward was an English composer of operettas such as Merrie England; his surname names a different nation, hence 'yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward was an English composer whose surname is a nationality.

clue.text: Announced shortened viva relating to PhD?

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: shortened is docked and a viva is an oral exam, giving docked oral

explanation.surface: Notice is given that a doctoral oral examination will be cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: DOCKED ORAL, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A PhD is a doctorate, so doctoral work is that done for the degree.

clue.text: Wicked leader ousted from small capital, with support of America

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the others
the leader of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: mini means small
Quito is the capital of Ecuador
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: An evil ruler is driven from a minor capital with American backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from MINI to leave INI, then QUITO, the capital of Ecuador, and US below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquitous means grossly unfair or sinful.

clue.text: Bug and another insect feel pain

parts.note: the ant is an insect, another one beside the bug
to agonise is to suffer anguish

explanation.surface: A list of insects that seem to suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' seems to be the first insect, but it is the verb, to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate them, provoke them.

clue.text: Wordy book's principal theme briefly enthrals Isaac's boy

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so one piece is held inside the other
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the thrust of an argument is its main point
Esau was Isaac's son in Genesis

explanation.surface: A verbose book's central idea is captivated by a biblical son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the last letter of the main-point word, and 'enthrals' puts Isaac's elder son, from Genesis, inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms is literally full of words, hence 'wordy'.

clue.text: Soft, wet earth over waste ground?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the earth word is read backwards

parts.note: mud is wet earth
P is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: Soft wet soil spread across neglected ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a dump as ground where waste is tipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish tip is ground for discarding refuse.

clue.text: Old gunman moved stealthily, occupying landing stage

indicators.note: occupying means taking up the space inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage for boats
stole means crept, moved quietly

explanation.surface: A gunslinger crept onto a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistoleer is an archaic term for a soldier armed with a pistol.

clue.text: From purges, makes great profit

explanation.surface: Someone profits from carrying out purges.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is to rid of dirt or undesirables, and also, colloquially, to win a lot of money.

clue.text: Quick to mourn

explanation.surface: Someone eager to grieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means sharp or eager; as a verb it means to wail for the dead.

clue.text: Writer, one featured in issue an awful lot

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: issue means offspring, sons
a quill is a pen
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An author appeared in a magazine issue very many times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a magazine number, but means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Squillions is a joking term for an enormous, uncountable number.

clue.text: Afternoon snack consumed by old Frenchman, mostly?

indicators.note: consumed by means held within, so the eating word sits inside
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a Gaul was an inhabitant of ancient France
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: An ancient Frenchman eats most of a cake at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: GAUL loses its last letter to GAU, which holds ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich cream cake served with afternoon tea.

clue.text: Main cash supply of priest

indicators.note: supply read as supple, flexible, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The chief source of a cleric's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun but is read as 'supplely', loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a priest or healer in contact with spirits, and the adjective describes such a figure.

clue.text: Interesting dive, when turning upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a dip is a dive or plunge
as means when

explanation.surface: A diver turns over mid-plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having flavour, hence lively, engaging.

clue.text: Having run to the front, secure hut for farm-workers

indicators.note: to the front means the letter is moved to the start of the word

parts.note: to anchor something is to secure it
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: After running ahead, someone secures a farm shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancho is a hut or group of huts housing ranch labourers in Spanish America.

clue.text: Notice how to falsify car's mileage

explanation.surface: Advice on fiddling a car's odometer.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock is slang for to spot; to clock a car is to wind back its mileometer fraudulently.

clue.text: Rump may be cooked rare

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rump steak might be served rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rump' looks like steak, but means backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump is the hindquarters, the backside.

clue.text: Essentially a greyish-blue colour

explanation.surface: Describing a shade that is basically grey-blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by itself, intrinsically; perse is also an old word for dark greyish-blue.

clue.text: Cancel runs chalked up from several balls?

definitions.text: runs chalked up from several balls?

explanation.surface: A scorer erases cricket runs written on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; the score from it is the over's score.
explanation.definitionFit: To overscore is to strike out by drawing a line through; the runs from six deliveries make up an over's tally.

clue.text: I'll pay to get a bit of relief after dreadful bus rides

indicators.note: after means the next piece comes after the scrambled one
dreadful means awful, so the letters are badly scrambled
a bit of means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A passenger relieved after awful bus trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges BUS RIDES into DISBURSE, with R from 'relief' after it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pays out money disburses it, so the speaker says they will pay.

clue.text: Jabber in card game

explanation.surface: A talkative card player.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker is something that jabs or prods; poker is also a gambling card game.
